test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The height of a right circular cylinder is three times its radius. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 3696 cm², then the volume of the cylinder is equal to ({taking } pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
**Given:**

Height of the cylinder = 3 × radius.

Curved surface area (CSA) = 3696 cm².

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × radius × height.

Volume of the cylinder = π × radius² × height.

**Calculation:**

Let radius = r and height = 3r.

CSA = 2 × π × r × height

CSA = 2 × 22/7 × r × 3r

3696 = 2 × 22/7 × r × 3r

⇒ 3696 = 22/7 × r²

⇒ r² = (3696 × 7)/132

⇒ r² = 25872/132

⇒ r² = 196

⇒ r = 14 cm

Height = 3 × r = 3 × 14 = 42 cm

Volume = π × r² × height

Volume = 22/7× 14² × 42\)

Volume = 22/7 × 196 × 42

Volume = (22 × 8232)/7

Volume = 25872 cm³

**The volume of the cylinder is 25872 cm³.**
